mission_1.search: On the open map, BFS found a 13.5 m path while expanding 928 nodes, whereas A* found a path of the same length but only expanded 700 nodes, 228 fewer. Both algorithms find the shortest path because every move has the same cost. My bfs uses a FIFO deque, where frontier.popleft() removes the oldest cell first, so the goal is reached in the fewest possible steps. My A* uses a heap ordered by f = g + ctx.heuristic(cell), with Manhattan distance as the heuristic. Since Manhattan distance never overestimates the distance to the goal, A* still finds the shortest path. BFS explores outward in all directions without considering where the goal is, while A* picks the cell with the lowest f first. Cells moving away from the goal get higher f values, so many of them are never explored before the goal is reached.
mission_1.failure: On the constrained map, BFS found a 24.5 m path with 848 expansions while DFS found a 50.0 m path with 448 expansions. The DFS path is longer because my dfs removes cells with frontier.pop(), so it acts as a stack and keeps following the newest branch, while my bfs uses frontier.popleft() and reaches the goal along a shortest route. On the unreachable map, all four planners returned no_path (BFS, DFS and A* after 9 expansions, IDDFS after 231). The no_path status means the search checked every reachable cell and never found the goal, while resource_limit means it ran out of its expansion budget before finishing, so it cannot say whether a path exists. Claude wrote the four planner functions, and I ran the debugging checks and the offline evaluation and checked the results against my saved file.
